title: BioXArena: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Multi-Modal Biomedical Machine Learning Tasks
claim: A benchmark is a coherent system of curated tasks, domains, evaluated agents, controlled execution, and metrics that together enable holistic evaluation.
layout: 5 colored panels in a grid, (a) to (e), icon-labeled headers
description: A five-panel grid figure, with each panel in its own pastel color and a rounded border. Panel (a), blue, is Expert-Driven Curation and has four stacked rounded boxes: sources, ML and biology experts, unified public task capsules, and hidden private labels. Panel (b), green, shows nine biomedical domains in a 3x3 grid of icon-plus-label tiles, including Sequence (DNA), Single Cell, 3D Structure, Network Biology, Chemical Biology, Perturbation Dynamics, Phenotype Disease, Imaging Integrated, and Text Integrated. Panel (c), purple, lists the 18 agent configurations in four boxes: Minimal, Generic, Biomedical, and ML Coding, with subscripted backbone names. Panel (d), yellow, covers Execution, with a sandbox resources box and an output box showing Submission.csv leading to the held-out grader. Panel (e), orange-red, lists the evaluation metrics and the analysis outputs. The eye goes first to the colorful domain icons in (b), then to the colored panel headers.
caption: Overview of \bench. (a) Tasks are curated from journals, conferences, and public databases by ML and biology experts, then packaged as unified public task capsules with hidden private labels and graders. (b) The benchmark has 76 tasks across 9 biomedical ML domains. (c) The 18 configurations comprise seven Minimal runners, seven generic coding-agent configurations (OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code), two biomedical agents, and two ML coding agents. Subscripts identify the backend LLMs; see Figure [ref] for experimental results and App. [ref] for abbreviation definitions. (d) All agents run under the same controlled resource configuration and submit a submission.csv to held-out task-specific graders. (e) Nine evaluation metric types feed the leaderboard, domain heatmaps, failure taxonomy, and runtime and token analysis across all 18 agents.
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate machine-learning model building, yet biomedical benchmarks emphasize question answering, reasoning, and tool use or cover narrow slices of biomedical ML coding. We introduce BioXArena, a biomedical machine learning (BioML) coding benchmark for task-specific model building on heterogeneous, often multi-modal datasets. It contains 76 end-to-end tasks across 9 domains: sequence, single-cell, structure, network biology, chemical biology, perturbation dynamics, phenotype--disease, imaging, and text-integrated tasks. Each task packages primary-source data with hidden labels, held-out graders, and biology-aware metrics on a unified 0-to-100 scale; agents write runnable code, train models, and predict private test samples. BioXArena emphasizes realistic data interfaces: most tasks require agents to integrate multiple input sources, including 46 tasks that combine distinct modality families. We compare 18 harness--backbone configurations: general-purpose coding, biomedical, and ML agents plus our Minimal runner, all under the same controlled resource configuration. Codex with GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task-level average score of 73.91 among 18 configurations, closely followed by Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (73.79). Matched-backbone comparisons show higher observed scores for mature coding systems than for Minimal; seven Minimal backends characterize model differences under a fixed runner. Beyond the main leaderboard, ablations, robustness checks, and scaling, runtime, and failure-mode analyses characterize how backbones, scaffolds, budgets, and domains affect BioML coding performance, exposing modeling and execution gaps across agent and LLM backbone families.
